NKJV.1: “And Bezalel and Aholiab, and every gifted artisan in whom the LORD has put wisdom and understanding, to know how to do all manner of work for the service of the sanctuary, shall do according to all that the LORD has commanded.”
NKJV.2: Then Moses called Bezalel and Aholiab, and every gifted artisan in whose heart the LORD had put wisdom, everyone whose heart was stirred, to come and do the work.
NKJV.3: And they received from Moses all the offering which the children of Israel had brought for the work of the service of making the sanctuary. So they continued bringing to him freewill offerings every morning.
NKJV.4: Then all the craftsmen who were doing all the work of the sanctuary came, each from the work he was doing,
NKJV.5: and they spoke to Moses, saying, “The people bring much more than enough for the service of the work which the LORD commanded us to do.”
NKJV.6: So Moses gave a commandment, and they caused it to be proclaimed throughout the camp, saying, “Let neither man nor woman do any more work for the offering of the sanctuary.” And the people were restrained from bringing,
NKJV.7: for the material they had was sufficient for all the work to be done—indeed too much.
NKJV.8: Then all the gifted artisans among them who worked on the tabernacle made ten curtains woven of fine linen, and of blue, purple, and scarlet thread; with artistic designs of cherubim they made them.
NKJV.9: The length of each curtain was twenty-eight cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits; the curtains were all the same size.
NKJV.10: And he coupled five curtains to one another, and the other five curtains he coupled to one another.
NKJV.11: He made loops of blue yarn on the edge of the curtain on the selvedge of one set; likewise he did on the outer edge of the other curtain of the second set.
NKJV.12: Fifty loops he made on one curtain, and fifty loops he made on the edge of the curtain on the end of the second set; the loops held one curtain to another.
NKJV.13: And he made fifty clasps of gold, and coupled the curtains to one another with the clasps, that it might be one tabernacle.
NKJV.14: He made curtains of goats’ hair for the tent over the tabernacle; he made eleven curtains.
NKJV.15: The length of each curtain was thirty cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits; the eleven curtains were the same size.
NKJV.16: He coupled five curtains by themselves and six curtains by themselves.
NKJV.17: And he made fifty loops on the edge of the curtain that is outermost in one set, and fifty loops he made on the edge of the curtain of the second set.
NKJV.18: He also made fifty bronze clasps to couple the tent together, that it might be one.
NKJV.19: Then he made a covering for the tent of ram skins dyed red, and a covering of badger skins above that.
NKJV.20: For the tabernacle he made boards of acacia wood, standing upright.
NKJV.21: The length of each board was ten cubits, and the width of each board a cubit and a half.
NKJV.22: Each board had two tenons for binding one to another. Thus he made for all the boards of the tabernacle.
NKJV.23: And he made boards for the tabernacle, twenty boards for the south side.
NKJV.24: Forty sockets of silver he made to go under the twenty boards: two sockets under each of the boards for its two tenons.
NKJV.25: And for the other side of the tabernacle, the north side, he made twenty boards
NKJV.26: and their forty sockets of silver: two sockets under each of the boards.
NKJV.27: For the west side of the tabernacle he made six boards.
NKJV.28: He also made two boards for the two back corners of the tabernacle.
NKJV.29: And they were coupled at the bottom and coupled together at the top by one ring. Thus he made both of them for the two corners.
NKJV.30: So there were eight boards and their sockets—sixteen sockets of silver—two sockets under each of the boards.
NKJV.31: And he made bars of acacia wood: five for the boards on one side of the tabernacle,
NKJV.32: five bars for the boards on the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the tabernacle on the far side westward.
NKJV.33: And he made the middle bar to pass through the boards from one end to the other.
NKJV.34: He overlaid the boards with gold, made their rings of gold to be holders for the bars, and overlaid the bars with gold.
NKJV.35: And he made a veil of blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and fine woven linen; it was worked with an artistic design of cherubim.
NKJV.36: He made for it four pillars of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold, with their hooks of gold; and he cast four sockets of silver for them.
NKJV.37: He also made a screen for the tabernacle door, of blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and fine woven linen, made by a weaver,
NKJV.38: and its five pillars with their hooks. And he overlaid their capitals and their rings with gold, but their five sockets were bronze.

NASB.1: 'Now Bezalel and Oholiab, and every skillful person in whom the LORD has put skill and understanding to know how to perform all the work in the construction of the sanctuary, shall perform in accordance with all that the LORD has commanded.'
NASB.2: Then Moses called Bezalel and Oholiab and every skillful person in whom the LORD had put skill, everyone whose heart stirred him, to come to the work to perform it.
NASB.3: They received from Moses all the contributions which the sons of Israel had brought to perform the work in the construction of the sanctuary. And they still [continued] bringing to him freewill offerings every morning.
NASB.4: And all the skillful men who were performing all the work of the sanctuary came, each from the work which he was performing,
NASB.5: and they said to Moses, 'The people are bringing much more than enough for the construction work which the LORD commanded [us] to perform.'
NASB.6: So Moses issued a command, and a proclamation was circulated throughout the camp, saying, 'Let no man or woman any longer perform work for the contributions of the sanctuary.' Thus the people were restrained from bringing [any more].
NASB.7: For the material they had was sufficient and more than enough for all the work, to perform it.
NASB.8: All the skillful men among those who were performing the work made the tabernacle with ten curtains; of fine twisted linen and blue and purple and scarlet [material], with cherubim, the work of a skillful workman, Bezalel made them.
NASB.9: The length of each curtain was twenty-eight cubits and the width of each curtain four cubits; all the curtains had the same measurements.
NASB.10: He joined five curtains to one another and [the other] five curtains he joined to one another.
NASB.11: He made loops of blue on the edge of the outermost curtain in the first set; he did likewise on the edge of the curtain that was outermost in the second set.
NASB.12: He made fifty loops in the one curtain and he made fifty loops on the edge of the curtain that was in the second set; the loops were opposite each other.
NASB.13: He made fifty clasps of gold and joined the curtains to one another with the clasps, so the tabernacle was a unit.
NASB.14: Then he made curtains of goats' [hair] for a tent over the tabernacle; he made eleven curtains in all.
NASB.15: The length of each curtain [was] thirty cubits and four cubits the width of each curtain; the eleven curtains had the same measurements.
NASB.16: He joined five curtains by themselves and [the other] six curtains by themselves.
NASB.17: Moreover, he made fifty loops on the edge of the curtain that was outermost in the [first] set, and he made fifty loops on the edge of the curtain [that was outermost in] the second set.
NASB.18: He made fifty clasps of bronze to join the tent together so that it would be a unit.
NASB.19: He made a covering for the tent of rams' skins dyed red, and a covering of porpoise skins above.
NASB.20: Then he made the boards for the tabernacle of acacia wood, standing upright.
NASB.21: Ten cubits [was] the length of each board and one and a half cubits the width of each board.
NASB.22: [There were] two tenons for each board, fitted to one another; thus he did for all the boards of the tabernacle.
NASB.23: He made the boards for the tabernacle: twenty boards for the south side;
NASB.24: and he made forty sockets of silver under the twenty boards; two sockets under one board for its two tenons and two sockets under another board for its two tenons.
NASB.25: Then for the second side of the tabernacle, on the north side, he made twenty boards,
NASB.26: and their forty sockets of silver; two sockets under one board and two sockets under another board.
NASB.27: For the rear of the tabernacle, to the west, he made six boards.
NASB.28: He made two boards for the corners of the tabernacle at the rear.
NASB.29: They were double beneath, and together they were complete to its top to the first ring; thus he did with both of them for the two corners.
NASB.30: There were eight boards with their sockets of silver, sixteen sockets, two under every board.
NASB.31: Then he made bars of acacia wood, five for the boards of one side of the tabernacle,
NASB.32: and five bars for the boards of the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the tabernacle for the rear [side] to the west.
NASB.33: He made the middle bar to pass through in the center of the boards from end to end.
NASB.34: He overlaid the boards with gold and made their rings of gold [as] holders for the bars, and overlaid the bars with gold.
NASB.35: Moreover, he made the veil of blue and purple and scarlet [material], and fine twisted linen; he made it with cherubim, the work of a skillful workman.
NASB.36: He made four pillars of acacia for it, and overlaid them with gold, with their hooks of gold; and he cast four sockets of silver for them.
NASB.37: He made a screen for the doorway of the tent, of blue and purple and scarlet [material], and fine twisted linen, the work of a weaver;
NASB.38: and [he made] its five pillars with their hooks, and he overlaid their tops and their bands with gold; but their five sockets were of bronze.

ESV.1: “Bezalel and Oholiab and every craftsman in whom the LORD has put skill and intelligence to know how to do any work in the construction of the sanctuary shall work in accordance with all that the LORD has commanded.”
ESV.2: And Moses called Bezalel and Oholiab and every craftsman in whose mind the LORD had put skill, everyone whose heart stirred him up to come to do the work.
ESV.3: And they received from Moses all the contribution that the people of Israel had brought for doing the work on the sanctuary. They still kept bringing him freewill offerings every morning,
ESV.4: so that all the craftsmen who were doing every sort of task on the sanctuary came, each from the task that he was doing,
ESV.5: and said to Moses, “The people bring much more than enough for doing the work that the LORD has commanded us to do.”
ESV.6: So Moses gave command, and word was proclaimed throughout the camp, “Let no man or woman do anything more for the contribution for the sanctuary.” So the people were restrained from bringing,
ESV.7: for the material they had was sufficient to do all the work, and more.
ESV.8: And all the craftsmen among the workmen made the tabernacle with ten curtains. They were made of fine twined linen and blue and purple and scarlet yarns, with cherubim skillfully worked.
ESV.9: The length of each curtain was twenty-eight cubits,  and the breadth of each curtain four cubits. All the curtains were the same size.
ESV.10: He  coupled five curtains to one another, and the other five curtains he coupled to one another.
ESV.11: He made loops of blue on the edge of the outermost curtain of the first set. Likewise he made them on the edge of the outermost curtain of the second set.
ESV.12: He made fifty loops on the one curtain, and he made fifty loops on the edge of the curtain that was in the second set. The loops were opposite one another.
ESV.13: And he made fifty clasps of gold, and coupled the curtains one to the other with clasps. So the tabernacle was a single whole.
ESV.14: He also made curtains of goats' hair for a tent over the tabernacle. He made eleven curtains.
ESV.15: The length of each curtain was thirty cubits, and the breadth of each curtain four cubits. The eleven curtains were the same size.
ESV.16: He coupled five curtains by themselves, and six curtains by themselves.
ESV.17: And he made fifty loops on the edge of the outermost curtain of the one set, and fifty loops on the edge of the other connecting curtain.
ESV.18: And he made fifty clasps of bronze to couple the tent together that it might be a single whole.
ESV.19: And he made for the tent a covering of tanned rams' skins and goatskins.
ESV.20: Then he made the upright frames for the tabernacle of acacia wood.
ESV.21: Ten cubits was the length of a frame, and a cubit and a half the breadth of each frame.
ESV.22: Each frame had two tenons for fitting together. He did this for all the frames of the tabernacle.
ESV.23: The frames for the tabernacle he made thus: twenty frames for the south side.
ESV.24: And he made forty bases of silver under the twenty frames, two bases under one frame for its two tenons, and two bases under the next frame for its two tenons.
ESV.25: For the second side of the tabernacle, on the north side, he made twenty frames
ESV.26: and their forty bases of silver, two bases under one frame and two bases under the next frame.
ESV.27: For the rear of the tabernacle westward he made six frames.
ESV.28: He made two frames for corners of the tabernacle in the rear.
ESV.29: And they were separate beneath but joined at the top, at the first ring. He made two of them this way for the two corners.
ESV.30: There were eight frames with their bases of silver: sixteen bases, under every frame two bases.
ESV.31: He made bars of acacia wood, five for the frames of the one side of the tabernacle,
ESV.32: and five bars for the frames of the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the frames of the tabernacle at the rear westward.
ESV.33: And he made the middle bar to run from end to end halfway up the frames.
ESV.34: And he overlaid the frames with gold, and made their rings of gold for holders for the bars, and overlaid the bars with gold.
ESV.35: He made the veil of blue and purple and scarlet yarns and fine twined linen; with cherubim skillfully worked into it he made it.
ESV.36: And for it he made four pillars of acacia and overlaid them with gold. Their hooks were of gold, and he cast for them four bases of silver.
ESV.37: He also made a screen for the entrance of the tent, of blue and purple and scarlet yarns and fine twined linen, embroidered with needlework,
ESV.38: and its five pillars with their hooks. He overlaid their capitals, and their fillets were of gold, but their five bases were of bronze.

NLT.1: “The LORD has gifted Bezalel, Oholiab, and the other skilled craftsmen with wisdom and ability to perform any task involved in building the sanctuary. Let them construct and furnish the Tabernacle, just as the LORD has commanded.”
NLT.2: So Moses summoned Bezalel and Oholiab and all the others who were specially gifted by the LORD and were eager to get to work.
NLT.3: Moses gave them the materials donated by the people of Israel as sacred offerings for the completion of the sanctuary. But the people continued to bring additional gifts each morning.
NLT.4: Finally the craftsmen who were working on the sanctuary left their work.
NLT.5: They went to Moses and reported, “The people have given more than enough materials to complete the job the LORD has commanded us to do!”
NLT.6: So Moses gave the command, and this message was sent throughout the camp: “Men and women, don’t prepare any more gifts for the sanctuary. We have enough!” So the people stopped bringing their sacred offerings.
NLT.7: Their contributions were more than enough to complete the whole project.
NLT.8: The skilled craftsmen made ten curtains of finely woven linen for the Tabernacle. Then Bezalel decorated the curtains with blue, purple, and scarlet thread and with skillfully embroidered cherubim.
NLT.9: All ten curtains were exactly the same size — 42 feet long and 6 feet wide.
NLT.10: Five of these curtains were joined together to make one long curtain, and the other five were joined to make a second long curtain.
NLT.11: He made fifty loops of blue yarn and put them along the edge of the last curtain in each set.
NLT.12: The fifty loops along the edge of one curtain matched the fifty loops along the edge of the other curtain.
NLT.13: Then he made fifty gold clasps and fastened the long curtains together with the clasps. In this way, the Tabernacle was made of one continuous piece.
NLT.14: He made eleven curtains of goat-hair cloth to serve as a tent covering for the Tabernacle.
NLT.15: These eleven curtains were all exactly the same size — 45 feet long and 6 feet wide.
NLT.16: Bezalel joined five of these curtains together to make one long curtain, and the other six were joined to make a second long curtain.
NLT.17: He made fifty loops for the edge of each large curtain.
NLT.18: He also made fifty bronze clasps to fasten the long curtains together. In this way, the tent covering was made of one continuous piece.
NLT.19: He completed the tent covering with a layer of tanned ram skins and a layer of fine goatskin leather.
NLT.20: For the framework of the Tabernacle, Bezalel constructed frames of acacia wood.
NLT.21: Each frame was 15 feet high and 27 inches wide,
NLT.22: with two pegs under each frame. All the frames were identical.
NLT.23: He made twenty of these frames to support the curtains on the south side of the Tabernacle.
NLT.24: He also made forty silver bases — two bases under each frame, with the pegs fitting securely into the bases.
NLT.25: For the north side of the Tabernacle, he made another twenty frames,
NLT.26: with their forty silver bases, two bases under each frame.
NLT.27: He made six frames for the rear — the west side of the Tabernacle —
NLT.28: along with two additional frames to reinforce the rear corners of the Tabernacle.
NLT.29: These corner frames were matched at the bottom and firmly attached at the top with a single ring, forming a single corner unit. Both of these corner units were made the same way.
NLT.30: So there were eight frames at the rear of the Tabernacle, set in sixteen silver bases — two bases under each frame.
NLT.31: Then he made crossbars of acacia wood to link the frames, five crossbars for the north side of the Tabernacle
NLT.32: and five for the south side. He also made five crossbars for the rear of the Tabernacle, which faced west.
NLT.33: He made the middle crossbar to attach halfway up the frames; it ran all the way from one end of the Tabernacle to the other.
NLT.34: He overlaid the frames with gold and made gold rings to hold the crossbars. Then he overlaid the crossbars with gold as well.
NLT.35: For the inside of the Tabernacle, Bezalel made a special curtain of finely woven linen. He decorated it with blue, purple, and scarlet thread and with skillfully embroidered cherubim.
NLT.36: For the curtain, he made four posts of acacia wood and four gold hooks. He overlaid the posts with gold and set them in four silver bases.
NLT.37: Then he made another curtain for the entrance to the sacred tent. He made it of finely woven linen and embroidered it with exquisite designs using blue, purple, and scarlet thread.
NLT.38: This curtain was hung on gold hooks attached to five posts. The posts with their decorated tops and hooks were overlaid with gold, and the five bases were cast from bronze.

WEB.1: “Bezalel and Oholiab shall work with every wise-hearted man, in whom Yahweh has put wisdom and understanding to know how to do all the work for the service of the sanctuary, according to all that Yahweh has commanded.”
WEB.2: Moses called Bezalel and Oholiab, and every wise-hearted man, in whose heart Yahweh had put wisdom, even everyone whose heart stirred him up to come to the work to do it:
WEB.3: and they received from Moses all the offering which the children of Israel had brought for the work of the service of the sanctuary, with which to make it. They brought yet to him freewill offerings every morning.
WEB.4: All the wise men, who performed all the work of the sanctuary, each came from his work which they did.
WEB.5: They spoke to Moses, saying, “The people bring much more than enough for the service of the work which Yahweh commanded to make.”
WEB.6: Moses gave commandment, and they caused it to be proclaimed throughout the camp, saying, “Let neither man nor woman make anything else for the offering for the sanctuary.” So the people were restrained from bringing.
WEB.7: For the stuff they had was sufficient for all the work to make it, and too much.
WEB.8: All the wise-hearted men among those who did the work made the tabernacle with ten curtains; of fine twined linen, blue, purple, and scarlet, with cherubim, the work of the skillful workman, they made them.
WEB.9: The length of each curtain was twenty-eight cubits,  and the width of each curtain four cubits. All the curtains had one measure.
WEB.10: He coupled five curtains to one another, and the other five curtains he coupled to one another.
WEB.11: He made loops of blue on the edge of the one curtain from the edge in the coupling. Likewise he made in the edge of the curtain that was outermost in the second coupling.
WEB.12: He made fifty loops in the one curtain, and he made fifty loops in the edge of the curtain that was in the second coupling. The loops were opposite to one another.
WEB.13: He made fifty clasps of gold, and coupled the curtains to one another with the clasps: so the tabernacle was a unit.
WEB.14: He made curtains of goats’ hair for a covering over the tabernacle. He made them eleven curtains.
WEB.15: The length of each curtain was thirty cubits, and four cubits the width of each curtain. The eleven curtains had one measure.
WEB.16: He coupled five curtains by themselves, and six curtains by themselves.
WEB.17: He made fifty loops on the edge of the curtain that was outermost in the coupling, and he made fifty loops on the edge of the curtain which was outermost in the second coupling.
WEB.18: He made fifty clasps of brass to couple the tent together, that it might be a unit.
WEB.19: He made a covering for the tent of rams’ skins dyed red, and a covering of sea cow hides above.
WEB.20: He made the boards for the tabernacle of acacia wood, standing up.
WEB.21: Ten cubits was the length of a board, and a cubit and a half the width of each board.
WEB.22: Each board had two tenons, joined to one another. He made all the boards of the tabernacle this way.
WEB.23: He made the boards for the tabernacle: twenty boards for the south side southward.
WEB.24: He made forty sockets of silver under the twenty boards; two sockets under one board for its two tenons, and two sockets under another board for its two tenons.
WEB.25: For the second side of the tabernacle, on the north side, he made twenty boards,
WEB.26: and their forty sockets of silver; two sockets under one board, and two sockets under another board.
WEB.27: For the far part of the tabernacle westward he made six boards.
WEB.28: He made two boards for the corners of the tabernacle in the far part.
WEB.29: They were double beneath, and in the same way they were all the way to its top to one ring. He did this to both of them in the two corners.
WEB.30: There were eight boards, and their sockets of silver, sixteen sockets; under every board two sockets.
WEB.31: He made bars of acacia wood; five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,
WEB.32: and five bars for the boards of the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the tabernacle for the hinder part westward.
WEB.33: He made the middle bar to pass through in the middle of the boards from the one end to the other.
WEB.34: He overlaid the boards with gold, and made their rings of gold for places for the bars, and overlaid the bars with gold.
WEB.35: He made the veil of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen: with cherubim. He made it the work of a skillful workman.
WEB.36: He made four pillars of acacia for it, and overlaid them with gold. Their hooks were of gold. He cast four sockets of silver for them.
WEB.37: He made a screen for the door of the tent, of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen, the work of an embroiderer;
WEB.38: and the five pillars of it with their hooks. He overlaid their capitals and their fillets with gold, and their five sockets were of brass.

CSB17.1: Bezalel, Oholiab, and all the skilled <sup>[1]</sup> people are to work based on everything the LORD has commanded. The LORD has given them wisdom and understanding to know how to do all the work of constructing the sanctuary.” <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.2: So Moses summoned Bezalel, Oholiab, and every skilled person in whose heart the LORD had placed wisdom, all whose hearts moved them, <sup>ⓖ</sup> to come to the work and do it.
CSB17.3: They took from Moses’s presence all the contributions that the Israelites had brought for the task of making the sanctuary. Meanwhile, the people continued to bring freewill offerings morning after morning.
CSB17.4: Then all the artisans who were doing all the work for the sanctuary came one by one from the work they were doing
CSB17.5: and said to Moses, “The people are bringing more than is needed <sup>ⓗ</sup> for the construction of the work the LORD commanded to be done.”
CSB17.6: After Moses gave an order, they sent a proclamation throughout the camp: “Let no man or woman make anything else as an offering for the sanctuary.” So the people stopped.
CSB17.7: The materials were sufficient for them to do all the work. There was more than enough.
CSB17.8: All <sup>ⓘ</sup> the skilled artisans <sup>[2]</sup> among those doing the work made the tabernacle with ten curtains. Bezalel made them of finely spun linen, as well as blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, with a design of cherubim worked into them.
CSB17.9: Each curtain was forty-two feet <sup>[3]</sup> long and six feet <sup>[4]</sup> wide; all the curtains had the same measurements.
CSB17.10: He joined five of the curtains to each other, and the other five curtains he joined to each other.
CSB17.11: He made loops of blue yarn on the edge of the last curtain in the first set and did the same on the edge of the outermost curtain in the second set.
CSB17.12: He made fifty loops on the one curtain and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain in the second set, so that the loops lined up with each other.
CSB17.13: He also made fifty gold clasps and joined the curtains to each other, so that the tabernacle became a single unit.
CSB17.14: He made curtains of goat hair for a tent over the tabernacle; he made eleven of them.
CSB17.15: Each curtain was forty-five feet <sup>[5]</sup> long and six feet wide. All eleven curtains had the same measurements.
CSB17.16: He joined five of the curtains together, and the other six together.
CSB17.17: He made fifty loops on the edge of the outermost curtain in the first set and fifty loops on the edge of the corresponding curtain in the second set.
CSB17.18: He made fifty bronze clasps to join the tent together as a single unit.
CSB17.19: He also made a covering for the tent from ram skins dyed red and a covering of fine leather <sup>[6]</sup> on top of it.
CSB17.20: He <sup>ⓙ</sup> made upright supports <sup>[7]</sup> of acacia wood for the tabernacle.
CSB17.21: Each support was fifteen feet <sup>[8]</sup> long and twenty-seven inches <sup>[9]</sup> wide.
CSB17.22: Each support had two tenons for joining one to another. He did the same for all the supports of the tabernacle.
CSB17.23: He made supports for the tabernacle as follows: twenty for the south side,
CSB17.24: and he made forty silver bases to put under the twenty supports, two bases under the first support for its two tenons, and two bases under each of the following supports for their two tenons;
CSB17.25: for the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, he made twenty supports,
CSB17.26: with their forty silver bases, two bases under the first support and two bases under each of the following ones;
CSB17.27: and for the back of the tabernacle, on the west side, he made six supports.
CSB17.28: He also made two additional supports for the two back corners of the tabernacle.
CSB17.29: They were paired at the bottom and joined together <sup>[10]</sup> at the <sup>[11]</sup> top in a single ring. This is what he did with both of them for the two corners.
CSB17.30: So there were eight supports with their sixteen silver bases, two bases under each one.
CSB17.31: He made five crossbars of acacia wood for the supports on one side of the tabernacle,
CSB17.32: five crossbars for the supports on the other side of the tabernacle, and five crossbars for those at the back of the tabernacle on the west.
CSB17.33: He made the central crossbar run through the middle of the supports from one end to the other.
CSB17.34: He overlaid them with gold and made their rings out of gold as holders for the crossbars. He also overlaid the crossbars with gold.
CSB17.35: Then <sup>ⓚ</sup> he made the curtain with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen. He made it with a design of cherubim worked into it.
CSB17.36: He made four pillars of acacia wood for it and overlaid them with gold; their hooks were of gold. And he cast four silver bases for the pillars.
CSB17.37: He made a screen embroidered <sup>[12]</sup> with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen for the entrance to the tent,
CSB17.38: together with its five pillars and their hooks. He overlaid the tops of the pillars and their bands with gold, but their five bases were bronze.

AMP.1: "Bezalel and Oholiab, and every skilled person in whom the LORD has put ability and understanding to know how to do all the work in the construction of the sanctuary, shall work according to all that the LORD has commanded."
AMP.2: So Moses called Bezalel and Oholiab and every skilled person in whom the LORD had put ability, everyone whose heart stirred him, to come to do the work.
AMP.3: They received from Moses all the offerings which the Israelites had brought for the construction of the sanctuary, to prepare it for service. And they continued to bring him freewill (voluntary) offerings every morning.
AMP.4: And all the skilled men who were doing all the work on the sanctuary came, each one from the work which he was doing,
AMP.5: and they said to Moses, "The people are bringing much more than enough for the construction work which the LORD commanded us to do."
AMP.6: So Moses issued a command, and it was proclaimed throughout the camp, "Let neither man nor woman do any more work for the sanctuary offering." So the people were restrained from bringing anything more;
AMP.7: for the material they had was sufficient and more than enough to do all the work.
AMP.8: All the skilled men among them who were doing the work on the tabernacle made ten curtains of fine twisted linen and blue, purple, and scarlet fabric, with cherubim [worked into them], the work of an embroiderer, Bezalel made them.
AMP.9: Each curtain was twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide; all the curtains were one size.
AMP.10: Bezalel joined five curtains one to another, and [the other] five curtains he joined one to another.
AMP.11: He made loops of blue on the edge of the outermost curtain in the first set; he also did this on the edge of the curtain that was outermost in the second set.
AMP.12: He made fifty loops in the one curtain [of the first set] and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain which was in the second set; the loops were opposite one another.
AMP.13: He made fifty gold hooks and joined the curtains together with the hooks, so that the tabernacle became a unit.
AMP.14: Then he made curtains of goats' hair for a tent over the tabernacle; he made eleven curtains in all.
AMP.15: Each curtain was thirty cubits long and four cubits wide; the eleven curtains were of equal size.
AMP.16: Bezalel joined five curtains by themselves and [the other] six curtains by themselves.
AMP.17: He made fifty loops on the edge of the outermost curtain in the first set, and he made fifty loops on the edge of the outermost curtain of the second set.
AMP.18: He made fifty bronze hooks to join the tent together into a unit.
AMP.19: He made a [third] covering for the tent of rams' skins dyed red, and above it a [fourth] covering of porpoise skins.
AMP.20: Bezalel made boards of acacia wood for the upright framework of the tabernacle.
AMP.21: Each board was ten cubits long and one and a half cubits wide.
AMP.22: Each board had two tenons (dovetails), fitted to one another; he did this for all the boards of the tabernacle.
AMP.23: And [this is how] he made the boards [for frames] for the tabernacle: twenty boards for the south side;
AMP.24: and he made under the twenty boards forty silver sockets; two sockets under one board for its two tenons (dovetails), and two sockets under another board for its two tenons.
AMP.25: For the other side of the tabernacle, the north side, he made twenty boards,
AMP.26: and their forty silver sockets; two sockets under [the end of] each board.
AMP.27: And for the rear of the tabernacle, to the west, he made six [frame] boards.
AMP.28: And he made two boards for each corner of the tabernacle in the rear.
AMP.29: They were separate below, but linked together at the top with one ring; thus he made both of them in both corners.
AMP.30: There were eight boards with sixteen silver sockets, and under [the end of] each board two sockets.
AMP.31: Bezalel made bars of acacia wood, five for the [frame] boards of the one side of the tabernacle,
AMP.32: and five bars for the boards of the tabernacle's other side, and five bars for the boards at the rear side to the west.
AMP.33: And he made the middle bar pass through [horizontally] halfway up the boards from one end to the other.
AMP.34: He overlaid the boards and the bars with gold and made their rings of gold as holders for the bars.
AMP.35: Further, Bezalel made the veil of blue and purple and scarlet fabric, and fine twisted linen; he made it with cherubim, the work of an embroiderer.
AMP.36: For the veil (partition curtain) he made four support poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold; their hooks were gold, and he cast for them four silver sockets.
AMP.37: He made a screen (curtain) for the doorway of the tent, of blue, purple, and scarlet fabric, and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer;
AMP.38: and [he made] the five support poles with their hooks, and overlaid their [ornamental] tops and connecting rings with gold; but their five sockets were bronze.

NIV.1: 36 So Bezalel, Oholiab and every skilled person to whom the Lord has given skill and ability to know how to carry out all the work of constructing the sanctuary are to do the work just as the Lord has commanded.”
NIV.2: Then Moses summoned Bezalel and Oholiab and every skilled person to whom the Lord had given ability and who was willing to come and do the work.
NIV.3: They received from Moses all the offerings the Israelites had brought to carry out the work of constructing the sanctuary. And the people continued to bring freewill offerings morning after morning.
NIV.4: So all the skilled craftsmen who were doing all the work on the sanctuary left their work
NIV.5: and said to Moses, “The people are bringing more than enough for doing the work the Lord commanded to be done.”
NIV.6: Then Moses gave an order and they sent this word throughout the camp: “No man or woman is to make anything else as an offering for the sanctuary.” And so the people were restrained from bringing more,
NIV.7: because what they already had was more than enough to do all the work.
NIV.8:
The Tabernacle
All the skilled men among the workmen made the tabernacle with ten curtains of finely twisted linen and blue, purple and scarlet yarn, with cherubim worked into them by a skilled craftsman.
NIV.9: All the curtains were the same size—twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide.
NIV.10: They joined five of the curtains together and did the same with the other five.
NIV.11: Then they made loops of blue material along the edge of the end curtain in one set, and the same was done with the end curtain in the other set.
NIV.12: They also made fifty loops on one curtain and fifty loops on the end curtain of the other set, with the loops opposite each other.
NIV.13: Then they made fifty gold clasps and used them to fasten the two sets of curtains together so that the tabernacle was a unit.
NIV.14: They made curtains of goat hair for the tent over the tabernacle—eleven altogether.
NIV.15: All eleven curtains were the same size—thirty cubits long and four cubits wide.
NIV.16: They joined five of the curtains into one set and the other six into another set.
NIV.17: Then they made fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in one set and also along the edge of the end curtain in the other set.
NIV.18: They made fifty bronze clasps to fasten the tent together as a unit.
NIV.19: Then they made for the tent a covering of ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of hides of sea cows.
NIV.20: They made upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle.
NIV.21: Each frame was ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide,
NIV.22: with two projections set parallel to each other. They made all the frames of the tabernacle in this way.
NIV.23: They made twenty frames for the south side of the tabernacle
NIV.24: and made forty silver bases to go under them—two bases for each frame, one under each projection.
NIV.25: For the other side, the north side of the tabernacle, they made twenty frames
NIV.26: and forty silver bases—two under each frame.
NIV.27: They made six frames for the far end, that is, the west end of the tabernacle,
NIV.28: and two frames were made for the corners of the tabernacle at the far end.
NIV.29: At these two corners the frames were double from the bottom all the way to the top and fitted into a single ring; both were made alike.
NIV.30: So there were eight frames and sixteen silver bases—two under each frame.
NIV.31: They also made crossbars of acacia wood: five for the frames on one side of the tabernacle,
NIV.32: five for those on the other side, and five for the frames on the west, at the far end of the tabernacle.
NIV.33: They made the center crossbar so that it extended from end to end at the middle of the frames.
NIV.34: They overlaid the frames with gold and made gold rings to hold the crossbars. They also overlaid the crossbars with gold.
NIV.35: They made the curtain of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, with cherubim worked into it by a skilled craftsman.
NIV.36: They made four posts of acacia wood for it and overlaid them with gold. They made gold hooks for them and cast their four silver bases.
NIV.37: For the entrance to the tent they made a curtain of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen—the work of an embroiderer;
NIV.38: and they made five posts with hooks for them. They overlaid the tops of the posts and their bands with gold and made their five bases of bronze.

MSG.1: "Bezalel and Oholiab, along with everyone whom God has given the skill and know-how for making everything involved in the worship of the Sanctuary as commanded by God, are to start to work."
MSG.2: Moses summoned Bezalel and Oholiab along with all whom God had gifted with the ability to work skillfully with their hands. The men were eager to get started and engage in the work.
MSG.3: They took from Moses all the offerings that the Israelites had brought for the work of constructing the Sanctuary. The people kept on bringing in their freewill offerings, morning after morning.
MSG.4: All the artisans who were at work making everything involved in constructing the Sanctuary came, one after another,
MSG.5: to Moses, saying, "The people are bringing more than enough for doing this work that God has commanded us to do!"
MSG.6:
So Moses sent out orders through the camp: "Men! Women! No more offerings for the building of the Sanctuary!"
The people were ordered to stop bringing offerings!
MSG.7: There was plenty of material for all the work to be done. Enough and more than enough.
MSG.8: Then all the skilled artisans on The Dwelling made ten tapestries of fine twisted linen and blue, purple, and scarlet fabric with an angel-cherubim design worked into the material.
MSG.9: Each panel of tapestry was forty-six feet long and six feet wide.
MSG.10: Five of the panels were joined together, and then the other five.
MSG.11: Loops of blue were made along the edge of the outside panel of the first set, and the same on the outside panel of the second set.
MSG.12: They made fifty loops on each panel, with the loops opposite each other.
MSG.13: Then they made fifty gold clasps and joined the tapestries together so that The Dwelling was one whole.
MSG.14: Next they made tapestries of woven goat hair for a tent that would cover The Dwelling. They made eleven panels of these tapestries.
MSG.15: The length of each panel was forty-five feet long and six feet wide.
MSG.16: They joined five of the panels together, and then the other six,
MSG.17: by making fifty loops along the edge of the end panel and fifty loops along the edge of the joining panel,
MSG.18: then making fifty clasps of bronze, connecting the clasps to the loops, bringing the tent together.
MSG.19: They finished it off by covering the tapestries with tanned rams' skins dyed red, and covered that with dolphin skins.
MSG.20: They framed The Dwelling with vertical planks of acacia wood,
MSG.21: each section of frame fifteen feet long and two and a quarter feet wide,
MSG.22: with two pegs for securing them. They made all the frames identical:
MSG.23: twenty frames for the south side,
MSG.24: with forty silver sockets to receive the two tenons from each of the twenty frames;
MSG.25: they repeated that construction on the north side of The Dwelling.
MSG.27: For the rear of The Dwelling facing west, they made six frames,
MSG.28: with two additional frames for the rear corners.
MSG.29: Both of the two corner frames were double in thickness from top to bottom and fit into a single ring
MSG.30: —eight frames altogether with sixteen sockets of silver, two under each frame.
MSG.31: They made crossbars of acacia wood, five for the frames on one side of The Dwelling,
MSG.32: five for the other side, and five for the back side facing west.
MSG.33: The center crossbar ran from end to end halfway up the frames.
MSG.34: They covered the frames with a veneer of gold, made gold rings to hold the crossbars, and covered the crossbars with a veneer of gold.
MSG.35: They made the curtain of blue, purple, and scarlet material and fine twisted linen. They wove a design of angel-cherubim into it.
MSG.36: They made four posts of acacia wood, covered them with a veneer of gold, and cast four silver bases for them.
MSG.37: They made a screen for the door of the tent, woven from blue, purple, and scarlet material and fine twisted linen with embroidery.
MSG.38: They framed the weaving with five poles of acacia wood covered with a veneer of gold, and made gold hooks to hang the weaving and five bronze bases for the poles.
